# Re-entry Navigation Case Plan: Chance Simmons

## Executive Summary & Clinical Assessment
Participant Chance Simmons is a 40-year-old male under SCDC Reentry Parole Supervision returning to Charleston after serving nearly 20 continuous years of incarceration from age 17. His score-based risk level is **HIGH (23/43)**, heavily weighted by static criminal history and dynamic deficits in **Education/Employment (7/9)**, **Leisure/Recreation (2/2)**, and **Companions (3/4)**. 

Crucially, Chance presents with exceptional protective strengths: **0/4 in Procriminal Attitude** (demonstrates genuine remorse, full accountability, and proactive seeking of psychological counseling) and **0/4 in Family/Marital** (resides in a highly supportive, stable parental home on Johns Island). He has no active acute housing or substance crises.

## Facilitation & CBT Coaching Strategy
- **Modeling Neutrality & Relational Tone:** Adopt an appreciative, encouraging, peer-level coaching tone. Chance is highly sensitive to authority and eager to please; avoid confrontational tactics or power struggles.
- **Targeting Dynamic Criminogenic Needs:**
  1. *Education/Employment:* Transition GED foundation into practical workplace habits, digital literacy, and first-ever community job placement.
  2. *Leisure/Recreation:* Restructure idle TV time into structured daily routines, trade training, and family-oriented prosocial activities.
  3. *Companions:* Insulate against negative neighborhood peer networks by reinforcing family protective factors and workplace social integration.
- **Impatience Management:** When minor impatience surfaces around job search pacing, validate his eagerness to earn while using CBT thought-mapping to highlight incremental progress.

## 90-Day Action Roadmap
1. **Weeks 1–2 (Stabilization & Licensing):** Connect with Father to Father Project for beginner's permit advancement to full driver's license; set up CARTA transit schedules from Johns Island.
2. **Weeks 3–6 (Digital Literacy & Job Preparation):** Conduct 1-on-1 digital application practice; submit tailored applications to local Fair-Chance trade and logistics partners.
3. **Weeks 7–12 (Placement & Maintenance):** Secure entry-level employment; monitor initial supervisor interactions; establish ongoing relapse prevention check-ins.

# My Fresh Start Action & Resource Guide: Chance Simmons

## Welcome to Your Fresh Start!
Chance, your commitment to taking full accountability and building a clean, successful future is truly inspiring. With the solid support of your family on Johns Island and your dedication to learning, you are positioned for long-term success. This guide outlines your personalized steps to secure your driver's license, master job applications, and launch your trade career.

---

## Local Community Resources & Support

### 1. Driver's License & Family Support
* **Center for Fathering / Father to Father Project**
  * **Address:** 4925 Lacross Rd, North Charleston, SC 29406
  * **Phone:** (843) 744-2126
  * **Services:** Guidance on converting beginner's permit to full driver's license, driver education resources, and family stability coaching.
  * **Action Step:** Call or visit to schedule an intake for driver license restoration support.
  * [Visit Website](https://scfathersandfamilies.com) | [Get Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=4925+Lacross+Rd,+North+Charleston,+SC+29406)

### 2. Driver's License Reinstatement & DMV Services
* **SCDMV Regional Service Center**
  * **Address:** 3790 Leeds Ave, North Charleston, SC 29405
  * **Phone:** (803) 896-5000
  * **Services:** Official driving records, permit testing, and license issue processing.
  * **Action Step:** Work with your Navigator to review official driving records before scheduling road tests.
  * [Visit Website](https://scdmvonline.com/Driver-Services/Reinstatement) | [Get Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=3790+Leeds+Ave,+North+Charleston,+SC+29405)

### 3. Public Transportation
* **CARTA Transit Authority**
  * **Phone:** (843) 724-7420
  * **Services:** Fixed route bus service and express workforce shuttle connections across Charleston and North Charleston.
  * **Action Step:** Review bus route maps for connections from Johns Island to job locations.
  * [Visit Website](https://ridecarta.com)

### 4. Substance Wellness & Relapse Prevention
* **Charleston Center (DAODAS)**
  * **Address:** 5 Charleston Center Dr, Charleston, SC 29401
  * **Phone:** (843) 958-3300
  * **Services:** Voluntary peer recovery support, wellness coaching, and outpatient counseling.
  * **Action Step:** Keep contact info handy for voluntary wellness support as you enter the workforce.
  * [Visit Website](https://charlestoncounty.org/departments/charleston-center/) | [Get Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=5+Charleston+Center+Dr,+Charleston,+SC+29401)

---

## Target Fair-Chance Career Matches

### 1. Palmetto Logistics & Distribution Hub
* **Role:** Forklift Driver / Order Selector
* **Pay Rate:** $18.00 – $22.50 / hr
* **Shift:** Day Shift (6:30 AM – 3:00 PM)
* **Why It Fits:** Strong entry-level opportunity with clear daily structure and on-site OSHA certification training. Fair-chance employer evaluating candidates case-by-case.
* [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=warehouse+logistics&l=Charleston%2C+SC)

### 2. Lowcountry Framing & Carpentry Pros
* **Role:** Framing Apprentice / Jobsite Laborer
* **Pay Rate:** $19.00 – $25.00 / hr
* **Shift:** Day Shift (6:30 AM – 3:00 PM)
* **Why It Fits:** Excellent match for active physical work, practical skill acquisition, tool reimbursement, and rapid pay advancement.
* [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=framing+carpentry&l=Charleston%2C+SC)

### 3. Builders FirstSource
* **Role:** Load Builder I - Yard / Warehouse
* **Pay Rate:** Competitive Market Rate
* **Shift:** Day Shift
* **Why It Fits:** Physical material handling and loading in Johns Island / Summerville area with clear team expectations and entry-level stability.
* [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://careers.bldr.com/)

---

## Your 4-Week Milestone Checklist

- [ ] **Week 1: Foundations & Licensing Action**
  - [ ] Complete initial orientation with Navigator and review driving permit steps.
  - [ ] Contact Father to Father Project to request driver license coaching.
  - [ ] Establish daily schedule to replace TV downtime with morning physical exercise and digital learning.

- [ ] **Week 2: Digital Literacy & Application Practice**
  - [ ] Practice online application navigation and email usage with your Navigator.
  - [ ] Complete introductory resume highlighting GED, reliability, and trade enthusiasm.
  - [ ] Map out transit routes (CARTA / family rides) for target work zones.

- [ ] **Week 3: Employer Applications & Interview Prep**
  - [ ] Submit 3 targeted applications to fair-chance warehouse and carpentry partners.
  - [ ] Practice mock interviews focusing on positive attitude, reliability, and eagerness to learn.
  - [ ] Attend driver permit advancement appointments as scheduled.

- [ ] **Week 4: Placement & Onboarding**
  - [ ] Follow up on submitted job applications.
  - [ ] Complete prospective employer interview and onboarding paperwork.
  - [ ] Review workplace communication strategies with your Navigator prior to Day 1.

CASE MANAGEMENT BRIEF
Page 1 Reentry Case Management System
CASE MANAGEMENT BRIEF (STAFF-FACING
ROADMAP)
Integrated Clinical Reentry Case Briefing
Participant: Chance Allen Simmons DOB / Age: April 17, 1986 (Age 40)
Housing Status: Stable, living with family on John's
Island
Legal Status: Reentry Parole Supervision (SC Dept
of Corrections)
Completed Score: 23 / 43 (High Risk Band) Prepared By: Reentry Program Management
1. RISK PROFILE
Overall Risk Level: HIGH (Score-Based: 23 / 43). This score-based high-risk profile is dominated by a Very High
need in Education/Employment, severe static juvenile offense history, and unstructured leisure time, offset by
extremely strong protective strengths in family support and prosocial attitudes.
Criminogenic Domain Score Reentry Assessment & Clinical Indicators
1. Education / Employment (EE) 7 / 9 (Very
High)
Never employed in the community. Complete lack of
established work habits, resume, or supervisor relations.
GED completed in SCDC.
2. Criminal History (CH) 7 / 8 (High) Juvenile grand larceny in 2003, followed by rapid escalation
to armed robbery, kidnapping, and firearm offenses.
Incarcerated for 20 years.
3. Companions (CO) 3 / 4 (High) Knows quite a few active criminal associates. Lacks
established local prosocial, law-abiding close friendships.
4. Leisure / Recreation (LR) 2 / 2 (Very
High)
No participation in community activities. High amount of
unstructured idle time spent watching TV all day (vulnerable
to boredom).
5. Alcohol / Drug Problem (ADP) 2 / 8 (Low) Admitted drug use within the past year. Currently abstinent
at intake, but represents an active risk factor requiring
relapse prevention.
SIGNIFICANT PROTECTIVE STRENGTHS (COUNTERVAILING FORCES):
• Family / Marital (FM) [0/4 - Very Low Risk]: Resides in an exceptionally warm, supportive, and stable parental
home. Family acts as an active protective shield insulating him from criminal peers.
• Procriminal Attitude/Orientation (PA) [0/4 - Very Low Risk]: Deep, genuine remorse. Takes full responsibility
for his past crimes ('reckless choices that were entirely mine'). Highly compliant, cooperative, and motivated to
lead a legal life.

-- 1 of 3 --

CASE MANAGEMENT BRIEF
Page 2 Reentry Case Management System
2. BEHAVIORAL INDICATORS (HOW RISK MANIFESTS DAY-TO-DAY)
• Typical Triggers: Boredom and unstructured idle time (watching TV); direct contact with active criminal associates
in his immediate community; first-ever legal job seeking frustration.
• Escalation Tendencies: Historically demonstrated rapid behavioral escalation, progressing from vehicle theft in
2003 to armed robbery with a firearm by early 2004.
• Decision-Making Patterns: Learning patience ('No, I learned patience, but I still can get impatient every now and
again'). Prone to minor impatience when things are slow but shows strong self-reflection.
• Authority Response Style: Highly cooperative, polite, and respectful. Responds exceptionally well to clear
expectations, guidance, and counseling professionals.
• Thinking Patterns Detected: No active criminal thinking. Deep remorse and 100% accountability. Proactively
sought private psychological adjustment counseling upon release to make sure he adjusts properly.
3. PATTERN OVER TIME (LONGITUDINAL trajectory)
First arrested at age 17 in July 2003 for Grand Larceny. Placed on probation, but caught Armed Robbery and
Kidnapping charges on January 13, 2004, leading to immediate probation revocation. Adult conviction registered in
General Sessions in December 2005. Served nearly 20 continuous years in adult prison. Currently on parole
supervision with zero community recidivism post-release. This reentry program represents an intervention in a
severe, early-onset static violent pattern.
4. ACUTE / EMERGENCY NEEDS
No acute needs identified at intake. He has stable housing, no active substance abuse crisis, and no mental health
instability. Relapse prevention and standard urinalysis are recommended because substance use within the last year
is documented, but he is currently stable and abstinent.
5. STRUCTURAL STABILITY FACTORS (BARRIERS TO PROGRESS)
• Housing: Stable, supportive home with family on John's Island.
• License / ID: Beginner's permit only. Requires transportation support and driver's education.
• Education: GED held, but formal schooling ended at 7th grade.
• Employment History: None. Critical barrier. Total absence of vocational habits, supervisor experience, or
workplace routines.
6. LEGAL & PLACEMENT CONSTRAINTS
No pending charges. Subject to active parole supervision, including standard curfew, travel restrictions, and
scheduled check-ins. No Sex Offender Registry requirements.

-- 2 of 3 --

CASE MANAGEMENT BRIEF
Page 3 Reentry Case Management System
7. RESPONSIVITY & ENGAGEMENT PROFILE
• Trauma & Institutionalization: Serving a 20-year adult prison sentence beginning at age 17 has left significant
institutionalization trauma. Reentry planning must accommodate adjustments to modern digital systems, modern
workplace pacing, and public life.
• Engagement Style: Extremely high internal motivation, highly receptive to faith-based programs (e.g. Kairos) and
cognitive-behavioral modeling.
STAFF COACHING RECOMMENDATIONS:
• Utilize an encouraging, appreciative, and peer-level coaching style to reinforce his highly positive,
cooperative self-concept ('lovable and caring').
• Avoid confrontational or adversarial authority styles, as he is highly sensitive to authority and eager to please.
• Provide hands-on digital literacy and structured job-seeking assistance.
• Actively involve his supportive family in case planning milestones.

-- 3 of 3 --
